initialize.instructions: Obtains and renews the OAuth 2.0 token of one account. Call auth_get, then show the user the authorizationUri to open, or the userCode to enter at the verificationUri, and call auth_status until the flow is issued or failed. When redirectCaptured is false, ask the user for the URL their browser was redirected to and pass it to auth_resume. No tool returns the token itself.

tools.description: Show the metadata of the stored token: its type, when it was issued, what remains of its lifetime, whether a refresh token is held, and the granted scope. The token itself is never shown.
tools.name: token_inspect

outputSchema.description:
Printable metadata of the stored token, holding no secret.

It carries what the text rendering has always shown, so both
renderings agree on handing out nothing sensitive: the raw access
token comes from `token show`, and the refresh token from storage.

expiresIn.description: The lifetime granted at issuance, in seconds, when known.

issuedAt.description:
When the token was issued, an RFC 3339 instant in UTC, `null` when
unknown.

scope.description: The granted scope, when the server reported one.

tokenType.description: The token type the server issued, usually `Bearer`.

withRefreshToken.description: Whether a refresh token was stored alongside the access token.

outputSchema.title: TokenInspectOutput

tools.description: Start the account's OAuth grant, replacing any pending flow. Returns the authorization URI for the user to open, or the user code and the verification URI for the user to enter it at; a client credentials account is issued at once. The server stores the token as soon as the user consents: follow with auth_status.
tools.name: auth_get

oneOf.description: An authorization code flow: the user opens the authorization URI.
A device flow: the user enters the code at the verification URI.
A client credentials grant, issued at once.

TokenIssuedOutput.description:
The access token a grant or a refresh just stored.

Printed by `token refresh`, `auth resume`, and `auth get` when its grant
issues the token in-process.

expiresIn.description:
The token's lifetime in seconds as the server stated it, `null`
when it stated none.

withRefreshToken.description: Whether a refresh token came with it.

outputSchema.description: What `auth_get` answers: what the user must do next, never a secret.

authorizationUri.description: The URI the user opens to consent, on an authorization code flow.

receipt.description:
The receipt of a token issued at once, on a client credentials
account.

redirectCaptured.description:
Whether the server catches the redirection itself; when `false`,
the redirected URL goes to `auth_resume`.

userCode.description: The code the user enters, on a device flow.

verificationUri.description: The page the user enters the code at, on a device flow.

verificationUriComplete.description:
The verification page with the code already in it, when the
server offers one.

outputSchema.title: McpAuthGetOutput

tools.description: Report the flow auth_get started: none, pending, issued with the receipt, or failed with the error.
tools.name: auth_status

ErrorReport.description: The failure object a command prints instead of its output.

backtrace.description: The captured backtrace, when backtraces are enabled.

code.description:
The stable code of the failure, `null` when the binary gave it
none.

sources.description: The messages of the causes, outermost first.

oneOf.description: The flow waits for the user.
The token was issued and stored.

NoErrorCode.description: The empty vocabulary of a binary whose failures carry no code.

uri.description: The URL the browser was redirected to after consent, carrying the code.
